sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 21.03.2023 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, Vijayapur (for short, 'the Tribunal'), whereby the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.15,55,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire compensation amount.
2. The brief facts of the case are that:
On 09.03.2020 at about 03-30 a.m., the deceased Mrutyunjaya Hiremath was proceeding along with his friends in the car bearing registration No.KA-28/P-3964 to Manipal.

When they reached near Mulemane Village, on Yallapur-Ankola road, the driver of the car drove the same in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner,
lost control over it and dashed to the road side standing electric pole and caused the accident.
In the result, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:1584-DB husband of petitioner No.1/Mrutyunjaya Hiremath sustained severer fatal injuries.
He was shifted to the Solapur hospital.
Due to the accidental injuries, he succumbed to the injuries on 12.03.2020.
Thereafter, the claimants who are the widow and children of the deceased have filed a claim petition before the MACT, Vijayapur in MVC No.1464/2021.
3. After service of summons, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.
4. Defendant No.1 in her written statement has denied all the material averments made in the claim petition and also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
It was contended that there is no nexus between the alleged incident and the death of the deceased Mrutyunjaya Hiremath.
The car was duly insured with respondent No.2.
The driver of the car was holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
and prays for dismissal of the petition.

Respondent No.2 filed written statement denying all the material averments made in the claim petition and also denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased and admitted that the car was insured with respondent No.2.
It was further contended that the accident was not due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car and sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the pleading of the parties, the Trial Court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that Mrutyunjaya S/o Shankaraya Hiremath, died due to the actionable rash and negligent act of the driver of TATA Car Vehicle bearing No.KA-28/P-3964, in the motor vehicle accident on the date, time and the place as being asserted?

sentences.text: Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

3 . What order of award?
To prove the case, petitioner No.3 son of the deceased was examined as P.W.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 14.
Respondent No.2 got examined its officer as R.W.1 and marked Exs.R.1 and R.2.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to adduce any oral and documentary evidence on her behalf.

8. On the basis of the oral and documentary evidence of the parties, the Tribunal has answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.15,55,900/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum fixing the liability to pay the compensation on respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have filed this appeal.

9. The learned counsel Sri Bapugouda Siddappa appearing for the appellants has contended that at the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 54 years and he was earning Rs.15,00,000/-
per annum, as he was NC: 2024:KHC-K:1584-DB doing a business in the name of Shivashankar Mantap Karyalaya.
The claimants have produced Ex.P.9 VAT certificate.
Without considering this aspect of the matter, the Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.13,750/- which is on the lower side.

He further contended that in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others1, the claimants are entitled for future prospects and also in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others2,
the claimants are entitled for loss of consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel Sri Subhash Mallapur appearing for respondent No.2/insurance company contended that even though the claimants have claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.15,00,000/- per (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2018) 18 SCC 130 NC: 2024:KHC-K:1584-DB annum,
except producing VAT certificate at Ex.P.9, they have not produced any other documents to establish that he was earning Rs.15,00,000/- per annum.
They have not produced any other documents to show that the deceased was the income tax assessee.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.13,750/- per month.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the appeal.
11. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the judgment and award.
12. It is not in dispute that Mrutyunjaya died in a road traffic accident on 09.03.2020 due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-28/P-3964.

Even though the claimants have claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.15,00,000/- per annum, except Sumangala And Ors vs Drakshayanni And Anr on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51551508/
4 producing Ex.P.9, no other documents have been produced.

sentences.text: Considering the evidence of P.W.1 that the deceased was doing business of NC: 2024:KHC-K:1584-DB Shivashankar Mantap Karyalaya and considering the age of the deceased, we are of the opinion that the monthly income of the deceased can be assessed at Rs.15,000/- per month.
In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi, 10% of the income of the deceased is to be added towards loss of future prospects.
The Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards his personal and living expenses.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 54 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable to this age group is 11.
In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Magma, the claimants are also entitled for loss of consortium at a sum of Rs.40,000/- each.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and medical expenses are retained.
Accordingly, the compensation to which the claimants are entitled to is re
- assessed as follows:

- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:1584-DB A) Loss of dependency : Rs.16,33,500/-
(Rs.15,000/- + Rs.1,500/-
(10% of Rs.16,500/-
= Rs.16,500/- x 12 x  x 11)
B) Loss of Estate : Rs.15,000/-
C) Funeral expenses : Rs.15,000/-
D) Loss of consortium  (Rs.40,000/- x 4) : Rs.1,60,000/-
E) Medical expenses : Rs.1,24,624/-
 TOTAL : Rs.19,48,124/-
13.

To this extent, the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
( i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.19,48,124/-
together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.15,55,900/- granted by the Tribunal.
